summary: This document describes a workflow for adding internal cross-links to blog articles. The process involves selecting articles to work on, running a checking tool to find linking candidates, manually choosing relevant links based on content (not just rankings), inserting them inline in the prose using a Link component, adding reciprocal links in older articles, verifying the links work, and reporting what was changed.

explanations.16: The slug is a short URL identifier for an article (like 'reactions' instead of the full path). This command searches all blog and draft folders to find which article has that slug.
explanations.26: This command shows all files currently changed or newly added in git (the working tree), filtering to just index.md files in blog folders, and extracts just the file paths (the $NF part means 'last field').
explanations.30: This is a fallback that looks at the previous commit (HEAD~1) compared to the current one (HEAD), finding articles that were Added, Created, or Modified, in case the working tree has no changes.
explanations.36: This command runs a checking tool that reports which internal links already exist in an article, flags bad links with '!!' if they point to non-existent slugs, and suggests other articles that might be good targets.
explanations.44: The ranking system suggests links based on keyword overlap and shared tags, but this can be misleading — it might suggest unrelated articles just because they mention the same tool, while missing the obvious connection the writing is actually making.
explanations.50: The project memory map is a reference file that lists articles by their main category tag and series, helping you spot related posts that the automated ranking might have missed.
explanations.58: This means the link should go where the term is first mentioned in the actual body text, not collected in a separate 'See also' section at the end, because a different component already handles related links at the page bottom.
explanations.61: The Link component is already available globally in this project, so you don't need to write an import statement — just use it directly with the target slug and anchor text.
explanations.71: After adding links, you run the same check command on all affected articles (including the older ones you added reciprocal links to) to ensure every link points to a real, published article.
